avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inducer; significantly reduces letermovir levels and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue St. John's Wort at least 2 weeks before letermovir initiation and avoid during treatment

avoid_supplements.name: Rifampin/Rifampicin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inducer; substantially decreases letermovir plasma concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concomitant use; if tuberculosis treatment necessary, consider alternative antituberculosis agents

caution_supplements.name: Grapefruit supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase letermovir levels; minimal clinical impact with standard dosing
caution_supplements.action: Limit consumption; monitor for adverse effects if used regularly

caution_supplements.name: Echinacea
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 inducer; potential for modest reduction in letermovir exposure
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution and counsel on potential reduced efficacy

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases letermovir plasma concentrations and exposure
avoid_foods.action: Completely avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, and related citrus products during treatment

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase letermovir absorption; food effect varies depending on formulation and patient factors
caution_foods.action: Take with or without food consistently; maintain standardized meal patterns if possible

monitoring_notes: Monitor CMV viral load and clinical response to letermovir therapy, as supplement/food interactions may compromise antiviral efficacy in immunocompromised patients. Counsel patients on strict adherence to interaction avoidance, particularly with potent CYP3A4 inducers which may render letermovir subtherapeutic.
